text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Attorney-General Amos Wako promises in parliament that a code of conduct to govern political campaigns with a provision to disqualify candidates and parties prone to violence will be in place before next year's general elections.
- Giant milk firm Kenya Cooperative Creameries management vows to resist plans to decentralise its operations and warns the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) to keep off its affairs.

- The High Court gives a group allied to the Raila Odinga oppostion FORD-Kenya faction (Forum for the Restoration of Democracy) more time to file a replying affidavit in a case in which Labour Party Democratic officials are seeking to bar the group from taking over their party.
- Official Leader of the opposition FORD-Kenya party Michael Kijana Wamalwa protests against current insecurity in the country, saying it is a pity Kenyans are living in a state of fear.
- Spectre International is ordered to serve receivers of the controversial Molasses Plant in Kisumu with a suit challenging its sale.

- Councillor Dick Waweru of Nairobi becomes the first "executive" mayor in the country when in an unprecedented move, the full council meeting makes changes in which he effectively takes over the running of the City Hall from the town clerk and chief officers.
- The government has been called upon to curb the influx of counterfeit drugs entering the pharmaceutical market as a way of restructuring the medical sector.
